calls.summary: Danielle Fuchs called to set up allergy testing after months of seasonal congestion. Oscar explained the skin panel process and immunotherapy plan pricing, then booked her intake at the Plano Family Medicine location. She left satisfied with a confirmed date.

Marcus Whitfield asked about the medical weight loss program and whether GLP-1 medications were included. Lila walked him through the monthly supervised plan and nutrition coaching, then scheduled his first provider visit. He was pleased with the clear breakdown.

Priya Nandakumar phoned the 24/7 emergency room to confirm wait times before bringing in her father with chest tightness. Rosey confirmed minimal wait and directed her to the nearest Fort Worth ER. The call was reassuring and quick.

Gregory Alcott called as a new patient looking for a family doctor accepting new patients and an annual physical. Mary collected his full details, insurance, and preferred location, then scheduled his wellness exam at the Denton clinic. He confirmed the appointment before hanging up.

Tanya Brooks needed a walk-in urgent care visit for her son's suspected strep throat. Lee confirmed no appointment was required but offered to reserve a rapid testing slot, which she accepted for the Irving location. She thanked him for the quick help.

Hector Salgado called about his medication management follow-up in behavioral health. Sue verified his current prescription and confirmed his existing psychiatry follow-up was still on the calendar. He had a couple of billing questions she answered.

Rebecca Lindqvist reached out about confidential behavioral health support and a first psychiatric evaluation. Mike explained the initial assessment and treatment planning, then booked her new evaluation appointment. She appreciated the discretion.

Owen Hargreaves called to check on results from his prior allergy testing panel. Jennifer located the chart but could not release results by phone and asked him to wait for the provider callback. He was mildly frustrated by the delay.

Sandra Kepler disputed a charge on her medical weight loss program invoice, saying she was billed twice this month. Rose opened a billing review and promised a corrected statement within a few days. Sandra remained skeptical about the timing.

Curtis Delacroix complained about the long line at an urgent care location during his last walk-in visit. Oscar apologized and logged the feedback for the site manager but could not offer a same-day resolution. Curtis stayed unhappy about the experience.

Aisha Coleman wanted a quick school physical for her daughter before a sports deadline. Lila found availability was tight but scheduled a clearance exam at the Arlington clinic for the next morning. Aisha was relieved but wished it were sooner.

Vincent Marlowe called disputing a large facility fee from an emergency room visit after a car accident. Lee explained the auto insurance billing process but Vincent felt the amount was excessive. The call ended without a firm resolution.

Nadia Petrosyan wanted to cancel an upcoming medication management follow-up because she had moved out of state. Sue processed the cancellation and noted the reason in her record. Nadia was curt but the request was handled.

Bradley Nomura called after hours and was routed to voicemail while trying to confirm a workers compensation injury visit for a coworker. No agent picked up and the message went unanswered during the call. The intent was left unresolved.

Gloria Ashworth complained loudly about being transferred three times while asking about a routine physical and lab results. Jennifer tried to help but Gloria demanded a supervisor and stayed dissatisfied. The call ended with an escalation note.

prompts.question: Is the caller trying to solve a specific problem?
prompts.answer: Yes, the caller is a new patient seeking an initial Family Medicine office visit for routine health evaluation and establishing primary care with TotalCare, specifically interested in a time slot that fits their work schedule.

prompts.question: What are the caller's expectations?
prompts.answer: The caller expects to schedule a convenient appointment time, have their basic information collected quickly, and receive confirmation of the booking before the call ends.

prompts.question: How could the agent handle the call better?
prompts.answer: The agent should have proactively asked about the caller's insurance coverage or self-pay status to set proper cost expectations, and captured the caller's email address for appointment reminders and future communication.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling TotalCare, this is Marcus speaking. How can I help you today?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Hi, I'm looking to schedule an appointment for a family medicine visit. I'm new to TotalCare and need to establish care with a physician.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Great, I'm happy to help you get scheduled today. Can I get your full name please?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Sure, it's Jennifer Martinez.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Perfect, Jennifer. So you're interested in scheduling a Family Medicine office visit for a general health evaluation, is that correct?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Yes, exactly. I haven't had a doctor in a few years and I want to get back on track with my health.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Wonderful, we have excellent physicians here at TotalCare. Just to confirm, which area of North Texas are you located in?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: I'm in Plano, so I would prefer the Plano location if you have one.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Perfect, we do have a Plano location. Can I get your phone number so we can reach you if needed?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: My number is ****-****-7324.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Excellent, thank you. I have your phone number on file. Now let me check our availability for you.

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: How much is a Family Medicine office visit going to cost me?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: That's a great question, Jennifer. Self-pay visits typically run between 100 to 200 dollars depending on what services are needed during your exam. Do you have insurance coverage I should note?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: I don't have insurance right now, so I'll be paying out of pocket. That price range works for me.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Got it, so you'll be self-pay. I have an opening next Wednesday, October 25th at 2:30 PM with Dr. Patel at our Plano location. Does that work for you?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: That sounds perfect, I can make that time work.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Wonderful, Jennifer. So I have you down for Wednesday, October 25th at 2:30 PM at TotalCare Plano for a Family Medicine visit with Dr. Patel. You can expect the visit to take about 45 minutes to an hour. Is there anything else I can help clarify before we wrap up?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: No, I think that covers everything. Thank you for your help.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're very welcome, Jennifer. We're excited to have you at TotalCare. If you need to reach us before your appointment, just call back or visit our website. Have a great day.

callDetail.aiSummary: Jennifer Martinez called to schedule her first Family Medicine office visit at TotalCare's Plano location. Marcus collected her name, confirmed her service interest, verified her preferred location and ZIP code, captured her phone number, and booked her appointment for Wednesday, October 25th at 2:30 PM with Dr. Patel. Jennifer confirmed she would be self-pay, and the agent provided typical cost expectations. The call was efficient and professional, though the agent did not capture Jennifer's email address for appointment reminders or confirm her cancellation policy.

comment.author: Kyle Paklaian
comment.text: @Marcus, great job on the structure and pacing of this new-patient intake. Your greeting was warm, you repeated back all the key appointment details, and you set proper cost expectations when Jennifer asked. Two small coaching points for next time: ask for email upfront so we can send reminder confirmations, and mention what she should bring to her first visit or any prep steps. Both touches improve first-visit show rates and reduce no-shows. Nice work overall.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling TotalCare, this is Marisol. How can I help you today?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Hi, I'm looking into your medical weight loss program. I've never been a patient there before, just found you online.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Welcome, I'd be glad to help you get started. May I have your first and last name?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Sure, it's Danielle Foster.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thank you, Danielle. Our Medical Weight Loss Program is provider supervised and can include GLP-1 medications along with nutrition coaching. Have you tried a program like this before?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: A little. I was going through one of those online clinics for a while, but honestly the guys down the street kept switching my dosing and I never talked to a real doctor.
highlights: never talked to a real doctor

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: I understand, and that continuity matters. With us you meet a board-certified physician who monitors your progress in person at one of our North Texas locations.

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Okay, that's good. What does the program actually run per month though? I want to keep it manageable.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Of course. The supervised plan generally runs between $200 and $450 a month depending on whether medication is included, and we review the exact plan at your first visit.

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Alright. And I'm being upfront, I'm getting a couple of quotes right now before I decide.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: That's completely fair, Danielle. What sets us apart is the in-person oversight and no long commitment, you continue month to month based on your results.

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: That helps, because I didn't want to feel locked into anything. One more thing, could I also do allergy testing while I'm there? I've had issues all winter.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Absolutely. Our Family Medicine team offers allergy testing and immunotherapy, and we can add that to your visit so you see one provider for both.

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Perfect. I'd need something this week though, I'm traveling after Friday.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Let me find you an early slot. We have Thursday at 10 AM at our Denton location with Dr. Patel, would that work?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Thursday at 10 works. Let me just double check with my husband on the drive, but yes, book it.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Wonderful, I have you scheduled Thursday at 10 AM. What's the best phone number and email for your confirmation?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: It's 940-555-0173, and danielle.foster@email.com.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Got it. You'll receive a text and email reminder, and please bring a photo ID and any current medications.

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Great, thank you so much.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thank you for choosing TotalCare, Danielle. We look forward to seeing you Thursday. Take care.
highlights: look forward to seeing you Thursday

brandConversationRules: Intro and offer: Introduce yourself as TotalCare's AI scheduling assistant helping new and returning patients find the right care and book an appointment across North Texas. Mention that new family medicine patients are being accepted now and ask if they would like to get started.

Qualify one question at a time: Ask a single question at a time to understand what the patient needs, covering which type of care they are looking for (emergency, urgent care, family medicine, or behavioral health), the reason for the visit or symptoms, whether it is a new or returning patient, their preferred timing, and their ZIP code to confirm a nearby location serves them.

Estimate then book: Confirm a TotalCare location serves their ZIP, explain that final costs depend on the visit and their insurance so a specialist confirms details at check-in, recommend the most fitting appointment, propose a specific day and time, and confirm they will receive a reminder text before the appointment with a number to call.

qaPairs.question: Do I need an appointment for the emergency room?
qaPairs.answer: No, our 24/7 emergency rooms are open around the clock with no appointment needed and minimal wait times. If it is a life-threatening emergency please call 911 or go to the nearest ER right away.

qaPairs.question: Is urgent care walk-in or do I book ahead?
qaPairs.answer: Urgent care is walk-in with no appointment required for minor illnesses and injuries. If you would like, I can confirm the closest urgent care location and its hours for you.

qaPairs.question: Are you accepting new family medicine patients?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, our board-certified physicians are welcoming new patients across the Dallas and Fort Worth Metroplex. I can help you book a family medicine appointment at a location near you.

qaPairs.question: When is the Denton urgent care opening?
qaPairs.answer: Our new Denton urgent care is coming soon and opening this fall. I can note your interest and help you find a nearby location in the meantime.

qaPairs.question: How much does an emergency room visit cost?
qaPairs.answer: Costs vary based on the care provided and your insurance, so our team confirms the details at check-in. I would recommend booking a visit so a provider can give you accurate information.

qaPairs.question: Do you offer allergy testing?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, our family medicine team provides skin and panel allergy testing along with personalized immunotherapy plans. I can set up an appointment so a provider can evaluate your symptoms.

qaPairs.question: Can I get a school or sports physical?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, we offer quick clearance exams for students, athletes, and commercial drivers. Let me know your preferred day and I will find an available appointment near you.

qaPairs.question: Do you have a medical weight loss program?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, we offer provider-supervised weight loss plans that may include medications and nutrition coaching. I can book an initial consultation so a provider can build a plan for you.

qaPairs.question: Can I see someone for mental health support?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, our behavioral health team offers confidential evaluations, medication management, and other treatment options. I can help you schedule a private appointment whenever works best.

qaPairs.question: Do you handle car accident injuries?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, our emergency rooms provide trauma evaluation, imaging, and injury documentation for car accidents, slips, and falls. This care is often billed to auto or liability insurance, and I can help you get seen quickly.

qaPairs.question: Do you treat workplace injuries?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, we provide workers' compensation injury care with return-to-work documentation at our ER and urgent care locations. I can help you find the closest location for treatment.

qaPairs.question: Do you offer COVID, flu, or strep testing?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, we provide same-day rapid diagnostics for COVID, flu, and strep at our urgent care and ER locations. I can point you to the nearest walk-in location.

qaPairs.question: Can I get IV fluids for dehydration or a migraine?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, we offer IV fluids and infusion therapy for hydration and symptom relief. I can help you find a location where you can be seen today.

qaPairs.question: How many locations do you have?
qaPairs.answer: We have 15 or more locations across North Texas with over 100 board-certified physicians. Share your ZIP code and I will confirm the closest one for you.

qaPairs.question: Do you take my insurance?
qaPairs.answer: We work with many insurance plans, and our team confirms your specific coverage at check-in. I can go ahead and book your appointment so the office can verify your benefits.

qaPairs.question: Can I do a virtual visit?
qaPairs.answer: Depending on your care needs, our team can advise on the best option for you. Let me help you book an appointment so a provider can determine the right approach.

qaPairs.question: What are your hours?
qaPairs.answer: Our emergency rooms are open 24/7, while urgent care and clinic hours vary by location. Tell me your ZIP code and I will confirm the hours near you.

qaPairs.question: Can you help me manage a chronic condition?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, our family medicine providers manage chronic conditions along with everyday health needs. I can schedule an appointment so a physician can create a care plan with you.

qaPairs.question: Do I need a referral to see behavioral health?
qaPairs.answer: In most cases you can book directly with our behavioral health team without a referral. I can help you set up a confidential appointment right now.

qaPairs.question: How do I book an appointment?
qaPairs.answer: I can book it for you right here. Just share the type of care you need, your preferred day, and your ZIP code, and I will confirm a nearby location and time.

Yeah, I'm in Denton and I think I might have a sprained ankle from a fall this morning. I don't think it's super serious but it's pretty swollen and I want to get it checked out today.

I'm sorry to hear that. A sprained ankle is definitely something we can evaluate quickly at one of our Urgent Care locations. Do you have insurance coverage, or would you prefer to pay out of pocket today?
I have insurance but I'm not sure about my copay. How much does an urgent care visit usually run?
